subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI sessions with an OpenClaw auth-profile credential present, should the auth epoch track stable credential identity rather than the local credential storage source shape?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes an auth/session invalidation boundary where maintainers must choose how to balance continuity against detecting real or ambiguous credential changes.

options.title: Use profile identity as canonical when present
options.body: Ignore local CLI fingerprint source-presence churn when a selected auth-profile credential exists, while still invalidating on profile identity changes and bootstrap/no-profile local credential changes.

options.title: Adopt host-only Claude CLI policy
options.body: Treat the host CLI login as the sole auth owner for Claude CLI, likely through the open host-only PR after resolving conflicts and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed epoch semantics
options.body: Continue invalidating on any local credential source-presence change and document that continuity loss is an intentional auth-boundary tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Use profile identity as canonical when present
recommendation.body: Ignore local CLI fingerprint source-presence churn when a selected auth-profile credential exists, while still invalidating on profile identity changes and bootstrap/no-profile local credential changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The auth-change invalidation behavior appears to date to Peter Steinberger's CLI session auth invalidation commit, making him the best available routing owner for the policy question.
